notes:
Account summary: Parallax Helix is a mid-market SaaS company that embeds an AI product assistant into their analytics UI and runs a separate support-agent flow. They are migrating from another LLM API provider (initially OpenAI) and evaluating Redwood Hosted API as the replacement, with a near-term goal to move to Dedicated for predictable latency and cost.

Key constraints / asks:
- Must preserve prompt parity and minimize behavioral regressions for 12 high-value intents (billing, dataset-summaries, step-by-step troubleshooting).
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for short chat prompts; p50 < 120ms for embeddings/reranking flows.
- Throughput: mid bursts ~120 reqs/sec, sustained 40-60 reqs/sec during business hours.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement wants clear TCO vs current provider; target ARR band for Redwood: $100k-$300k.
- Security: SSO (SAML), SOC2 compliance, audit logs retained 90 days; optional KMS for key separation. Data residency: US only for analytics-derived PII.

Timeline / recent activity (bullet-style CRM notes):
- 2025-11-02: inbound MQL, initial intro call with Alyssa C. (AE).
- 2026-01-15: product demo of Hosted API + console; showed streaming and function-calling examples (linked gm thread).
- 2026-02-10: security questionnaire sent; Parallax returned basic SOC2 docs.
- 2026-02-20: kickoff POC (Fireflies ff_20260220_1122) — 2-week technical POC to validate prompt parity and latency on Hosted.
- 2026-03-03: POC checkpoint call (ff_20260303_3389) — identified regressions on 'billing explain' intent when switching models; SE triaged prompting/context-window differences.
- 2026-03-05: SE deployed a compat-layer shim to emulate their prior provider's injection behavior; partial parity achieved but 3 intents still divergent (see RDW-1423).
- 2026-03-08: internal pricing discussion with procurement; asked for Dedicated reserved pricing scenarios and burst policy for autoscaling.

Technical notes from SE sessions:
- Compat layer approach: token-preserving prefix injection + response post-process normalization. Team prefers not to rewrite all prompts. Marco (SE) proposed a small shim library (node/py) to map provider-specific function-calls to Redwood's function schema.
- Regression root causes: different default temperature / sampling on hosted model variants; slight tokenization differences causing parsed-number mismatches; truncation of long system prompts when moving to Dedicated quantized variants.
- Acceptance criteria for POC: 95% intent parity on labeled set of 2,200 test prompts; p95 latency below 350ms on Hosted; ability to switch to Dedicated with feature parity (KV cache, streaming).

Commercial / pricing notes:
- Procurement flagged current provider discount and wants equivalent committed-rate for Dedicated. Wants 12-month and 24-month reserved options.
- Asked for detailed per-token cost comparison and sample monthly bill model for 15M tokens/month.

Quotes / paraphrases:
- "We need prompt parity — dev team refuses to rewrite outputs for 12 intents." — Head of Product (call 2026-03-03).
- "If Redwood can show <10% increase in cost and equal/better latency we'll move to Dedicated." — Procurement (email gm_20260305_thread_77).

Next steps (explicit):
- AE (Alyssa) to deliver Dedicated pricing scenarios (3 tiers: small reserve, medium reserve, enterprise commit) by 2026-03-12.
- SE (Marco) to deliver compat-layer shim repo + runbook and execute full prompt-parity pass on POC dataset by 2026-03-25. (linked: drive://parallax/prompt-parity-runbook.md)
- Run extended A/B eval comparing outputs from current provider vs Redwood Hosted and produce mismatch matrix; raise any regressions as RDW tickets.
- Legal to confirm data residency clause and provide SOW template for on-prem/backplane KMS options.

Open blockers / risk profile:
- Prompt parity regressions (medium risk) — could delay decision if >5% critical-intent mismatch.
- Pricing delta — procurement will push back if committed pricing isn't competitive.
- Dedicated feature parity unknown for their streaming+KV cache behaviour — SE validation required.

Internal win signals:
- POC showed 85% parity after 1st shim iteration; product team engaged and willing to run deeper evals.
- Prefers Redwood UI for observability and token-level breakdowns; positive feedback on Console routing/fallback examples.

Related artifacts / references:
- POC ticket RDW-1423 (tracking billing-intent regression) and RDW-1478 (compat-layer integration failures).
- Pricing deck: drive://parallax/Redwood-POC-pricing-v1.pdf
- Prompt parity runbook: drive://parallax/prompt-parity-runbook.md

Short-term ask from AE: prioritize a Dedicated pricing scenario that matches monthly committed TCO within 10% of their current provider. SE ask: deliver a shim + automated eval harness for parity checks.
